text:
marta_sec: Quick FYI — kicking off AWS KMS integration for Redwood Private (VPC) control plane + data-plane. Need agreement on envelope key flow, rotation windows, and audit/logging expectations. tagging @kevin_infra @alex_dev for infra/serving runtime implications.

kevin_infra: SGTM. main questions: 1) KEK in customer account or ours? 2) who performs rewrap on rotation (control plane vs dataplane sidecar)?

alex_dev: Prefer customer-owned CMK (BYOK) in their account for Private. That avoids us holding KEK. But we need a consistent grant/assume role pattern to let control plane rewrap and dataplane decrypt.

marta_sec: Agreed on BYOK for regulated customers. Proposed model: customer CMK (KEK) in their account -> grants to our service principal for Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey; we only ever store encrypted DEKs (envelope). Dataplane instances in customer VPC use an IAM role that can call KMS in their account to decrypt DEKs.

kevin_infra: Sounds good. Two implementation notes: (a) control plane must not cache plaintext DEKs beyond request scope; (b) dataplane should prefer a cached DEK for active model sessions but have TTL and re-fetch on rotation.

alex_dev: For rewrap/rotation: customer triggers CMK rotation (or we advise schedule). When KEK rotates, we need a rewrap job to decrypt with prior KEK and re-encrypt DEKs with new KEK. Who runs that? If customer CMK is in their account, we can't keep plaintext long — so we should run a short-lived job in customer's account (via ephemeral task) that performs rewrap and writes new ciphertext DEKs to our control plane.

marta_sec: Proposal: use cross-account role: customer creates role with limited permission to call kms:Decrypt and kms:Encrypt, and a narrow S3/secret store write to send new ciphertext back. We run a scheduled rewrap lambda inside their account (owned by them) or they can run it manually. That keeps KEK plaintext confined to their account.

alex_dev: Implementation detail: for on-prem/private air-gapped we need an alternative: customer runs supplied rewrap tool on their side; we provide container binary that performs rewrap given access to KMS. Documented CLI workflow.

kevin_infra: Audit requirements: must capture KMS calls (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext/DescribeKey) in CloudTrail with global service logs and forward to our observability (only metadata, not plaintext). Also require CMK key policy to include our service principal and the cross-account role.

marta_sec: Confirmed. Add requirement: CloudTrail must have log-file validation enabled and put events in customer S3 + (optionally) forward to our ingestion via a signed endpoint for SOC-level correlation. We will never request access to S3 buckets, only ask for delivery to an endpoint.

opsbot: deploybot: New policy template created: arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/redwood-kms-rewrap-role. Policy allows kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:ReEncrypt*, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:DescribeKey limited to the CMK ARN.

alex_dev: RBAC side: control plane operators will need a scoped admin UI permission to kick off rewrap, view rotation status (no secrets). Add audit-log entries for who initiated rewrap. Keep UI action gated behind enterprise tier + consent from customer.

kevin_infra: Vulnerability/incident considerations: If we detect suspicious Decrypt calls (anomalous principal/timing), we need playbook: 1) immediately revoke service principal grants (via policy or disable key), 2) notify customer, 3) rotate DEKs and rewrap with new KEK if needed, 4) run forensic on CloudTrail logs. Is that acceptable?

marta_sec: Yes. Add to incident playbook: run a quick scan for leaked DEKs (artifact audit), generate short-lived lockdown credentials, and provide customers with timeline + signed statement. We should pre-bake Lambda to disable grants on request.

sara_platform: One more: latency/cost. Frequent rewraps are expensive (GenerateDataKey calls and Encrypt operations). Recommend rotation cadence defaults: DEK rotation every 90 days; KEK rotation as customer policy (we recommend yearly) — provide automated rewrap window with batch throttling and backoff.

alex_dev: For the serving runtime, we should support on-the-fly rewrap detection: dataplane receives 403 decrypt -> fetch latest ciphertext DEK from control plane and retry. Implement exponential backoff and eventual fallback to a compatible model variant.

kevin_infra: Clarify logs exposed to us: only metadata (operation, key_arn, request_id, principal). We must not request plaintext or raw DEKs. Also ensure our debug mode redaction blocks any base64 blobs in logs.

marta_sec: I'll draft a short security spec and a customer onboarding checklist: required key policy snippet, IAM role trust policy, CloudTrail settings, rewrap role ARN, and incident contact. I'll post it in #docs once ready.

alex_dev: Thanks. Can you include the sample key policy + role in the spec? I can start wiring the rewrap job and dataplane retry logic.

marta_sec: Will do. Target: share spec tomorrow EOD. Quick ask: anyone object to defaulting to BYOK for Private?

kevin_infra: No objections. BYOK is safer for compliance customers.

sara_platform: +1

marta_sec: Cool. I'll follow up with the draft. :white_check_mark:
